description: Where this board's build finds its tools, and nothing else.
Linux-native. KiCad is the distribution package, so kicad-cli and the
stock libraries sit on the system prefix and `pcbnew` imports from the
system interpreter's dist-packages - there is no separate bundled Python
to find. `cli` and `python` are bare command names on purpose: they
resolve through PATH, which keeps a fresh clone working on any machine
that has the packages, and the resolved absolute path is recorded in the
run's own provenance rather than frozen here.
Design rules, net classes, via sizes and clearances are deliberately NOT
restated here. Once this board has a project they live in the .kicad_pro
net classes, which is the same source the generator, the router and the
validator all read. A second copy of a threshold is a rival threshold.
This board has not been designed yet, so no path below points at a board
file. The tool identities are still the ones the board will use, and they
are recorded now so that a design run starts from a stated environment
rather than from whatever happened to be installed.

router.name: KiCad Routing Tools
router.development_checkout_note: Null on purpose. The router is a submodule of the toolkit at tooling/PCBA_AutoDesignAndTest/tooling/KiCadRoutingTools, pinned to a commit on its pcba-autonomy branch, so a recursive clone has it and no absolute path has to be true on more than one machine. This key survives as the development affordance it is: set it to a local checkout to test an unpinned router, and pcbqa.krt will prefer it over the submodule. Setting it to a path that is not a KRT root is an error, never a silent fall-through.
router.note: Resolved through pcbqa.krt: explicit override, then PCB_KRT_PATH, then this development checkout, then the router vendored into the toolkit as its tooling/KiCadRoutingTools submodule, then a single active plugin installation. With development_checkout null it is the SUBMODULE that resolves, which is what a benchmark run should use: a pinned router outranks whatever a particular machine has installed, so a result is attributable to a commit.

toolkit.note: The pinned submodule, and the only way this repository reaches the toolkit. No sibling checkout, no absolute path, no PYTHONPATH assumption.
